    - article:
      - heading "PLAYFAIR'S AXIOM" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Through a point P not on line ℓ, there is exactly one line through P parallel to ℓ.
      - img "Interactive fifth-postulate equivalence diagram": P n ℓ 10°
      - button "Animate":
        - img
        - text: Animate
      - heading "Conclusion" [level=3]:
        - img
        - text: Conclusion
      - paragraph: Exactly one line through P is parallel to ℓ. The other line intersects ℓ.
      - heading "LINKED EQUIVALENCES" [level=3]
      - paragraph: All three scenarios are equivalent.
      - text: 1 ⟷ 2 ⟷ 3
    - article:
      - heading "2 INTERIOR-ANGLE CONDITION" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If a transversal cuts two lines and same-side interior angles sum to less than 180°, the lines meet on that side.
      - img: α β ℓ m t
      - strong: α = 73° β = 65° α+β = 138° < 180°
      - img
      - text: "Result: The lines meet on the left side."
    - article:
      - heading "3 TRIANGLE ANGLE SUM" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The interior angles of any triangle sum to 180°.
      - img: 60° 50° 70°
      - strong: 60° + 50° + 70° = 180°
      - img
      - text: "Result: Triangle angle sum = 180°."
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: WHY IT WORKS
      - paragraph: In Euclidean geometry, each of these statements implies the others.
      - paragraph: 1 Playfair's axiom gives uniqueness of the parallel.
      - paragraph: 2 If same-side interior angles sum to less than 180°, the lines meet; if equal to 180°, they are parallel.
      - paragraph: 3 The triangle angle sum of 180° forces this behavior.
      - paragraph: Therefore, all three are equivalent to Euclid's Fifth Postulate.
    - article:
      - heading "▣ WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If same-side interior angles sum to less than 180°, the lines meet on that side.
      - img: α β ℓ m t
      - strong: 110° + 40° = 150° < 180°
      - paragraph: Therefore, lines ℓ and m meet on the left side.
      - button "Step-by-step reasoning⌄"
    - article:
      - heading "MISCONCEPTION WARNING" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: MISCONCEPTION WARNING
      - paragraph: “At least one parallel” is weaker than “exactly one parallel.”
      - img: P ℓ
      - paragraph: This could allow 0, 1, or infinitely many parallels. Euclid's postulate requires exactly one.

    - paragraph: Turn off one assumption and identify which conclusions no longer follow.
